transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
Voting has begun in Israel.
Many Israelis called today's election the most consequential in their country's history
after the last three years of war.
NPR's Daniel Estrin reports from Tel Aviv.
Israel is holding its first national vote since the Hamas attacks of October 7, 2023
years of war in Gaza, Lebanon, and across the region.
Those conflicts remain open.
Netanyahu is running for re-election with a promise to join forces with the U.S. to
launch new strikes on Iran if he is re-elected.
Most polls have shown Netanyahu and his far-right bloc trailing behind the center-right opposition
led by former military chief Gadi Isinkut.
It may take weeks to find out who will be Israel's next prime minister.
Researchers are choosing parties running for parliament.
After election day, party leaders will try to assemble a coalition.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again.
The case is the third time prosecutors have brought criminal charges.
The latest allegations unsealed in federal court in Washington Monday.
NPR's Ryan Lucas.
Comey faces two criminal counts in this latest case, one for the alleged disclosure of sensitive
information and the other alleging a conspiracy to disclose such information.
Now, court papers say this all dates back to October of 2016, so 10 years ago, when
Comey was still FBI director.
And the charges revolve around an article published in The New York Times on October
5th of that year about U.S. email surveillance.
Charges against Comey came on the same day that a judge found the Justice Department
unlawfully fired Comey's daughter from her job as a federal prosecutor in New York.
Montana's competitive first congressional district drawing prominent Republican figures
as election day draws closer.
Montana public radio's Clayton Murphy reports on Vice President J.D. Vance's visit to
a district that could help determine control of the House of Representatives.
In the past two weeks, President Trump, House Speaker Mike Johnson, and Vice President Vance
have stumped in Montana.
The message has been simple.
Get out and vote.
Vance's rally in an airport hangar was no different.
"Let's send a message to the patriots of Montana that in this state we believe in sovereignty.
In this state we believe in freedom."
Vance stumped for House candidate and former conservative talk radio host Aaron Flint.
His race against Democrat Sam Forstag, a former Forest Service smokejumper, is by most accounts
a toss-up.
About a quarter of the state's registered voters have already voted by mail.
Vance's next stop is Michigan, where several races are also considered toss-ups.
For NPR News, I'm Clayton Murphy in Belgrade, Montana.
And you're listening to NPR News.
A court hearing is set for this afternoon in a case involving some 20,000 people on
California's voter rolls.
The Justice Department wants any ballots from them set aside alleging they should not be
counted because they belong to non-citizen voters.
In a two-to-one decision last night, an appeals court dismissed a DOJ appeal in the case setting
up today's hearing before a federal district judge.
California officials say the list is unreliable and that it's not feasible to set aside the
ballots this close to Election Day.
Following lung cancer surgery, Megan Williams reports that Pope Leo has been cleared to
travel to South America next month.
Doctors say there's no medical reason Leo can't travel to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru
as planned.
The 71-year-old Catholic leader had part of his right lung removed on October 13th.
And left Rome's Gemelli Hospital four days later, waving to well-wishers outside days
earlier than expected.
The Vatican says tests confirmed the cancer was localized and no further treatment is
needed.
Leo has gradually resumed his duties, with rest built into his schedule.
He says he's looking forward to returning to Peru, where he spent some 20 years as a
missionary and bishop.
For NPR News, I'm Megan Williams in Rome.
The Milwaukee Brewers are within one victory of winning their first World Series title.
The Brewers have a three-games-to-nothing lead in the best of seven after Monday night's
10-to-one win over the Tampa Bay Rays.
I'm Giles Snyder, NPR News.

topics.text: Israel holds first national election since October 7 attacks, with Netanyahu trailing in polls
Justice Department brings third criminal case against former FBI Director James Comey over 2016 leak
Vice President Vance campaigns in Montana for House candidate Aaron Flint in tight race
Court hearing set on Justice Department demand to set aside ballots of 20,000 alleged non-citizen voters in California
Pope Leo cleared by doctors to travel to South America next month after lung cancer surgery
Milwaukee Brewers lead Tampa Bay Rays 3-0 in World Series after 10-1 win
